title: General Knowledge Challenge
description: Put your general trivia to the test with 10 classic questions spanning world records, landmarks, and global culture.
seoTitle: General Knowledge Challenge – Free Trivia Quiz | AI Quiz Arena
seoDescription: Take our quick 10-question General Knowledge Challenge. Test your trivia skills, view instant explanations, and beat your personal best.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean basin on Earth, covering more than 60 million square miles.

questions.question: What is the hardest natural substance found on Earth?
questions.explanation: Diamond is composed of carbon atoms arranged in a strong crystal lattice, making it the hardest natural mineral known.

questions.question: Which country gifted the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
questions.explanation: The Statue of Liberty was a gift of friendship from the people of France to the United States, dedicated in 1886.

questions.question: How many colors are in a standard rainbow?
questions.explanation: The standard visible spectrum consists of seven colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet (ROYGBIV).

questions.question: Which animal is officially known as the fastest land mammal?
questions.explanation: The cheetah can reach speeds between 60 and 70 mph (97 to 113 km/h) in short sprints.

questions.question: In which city is the famous Colosseum located?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum is an ancient amphitheater situated in the center of Rome, Italy, built under the Flavian emperors.

questions.question: What is the primary currency used in Japan?
questions.explanation: The Japanese Yen (JPY) has been the official currency of Japan since 1871.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure, which meteorologists use to forecast weather changes.

questions.question: Who painted the famous masterpiece 'Mona Lisa'?
questions.explanation: The Mona Lisa was painted by the Italian Renaissance polymath Leonardo da Vinci in the early 16th century.

questions.question: Which element does the chemical symbol 'O' represent?
questions.explanation: 'O' is the atomic symbol for Oxygen, atomic number 8 on the periodic table.
